findings: legacyImportSender.ts (bulk CSV import path) sends a payload with only orderId and amount, omitting the currency field that the v2 docs declare as 'always present' — the sender was never updated when the schema moved from v1 to v2.

consumer.ts calls payload.currency.toUpperCase() with no null/undefined check; when currency is missing (as it always is from the import path) this throws a TypeError and crashes, exactly matching the reported intermittent-crash-only-on-CSV-import-orders symptom.

There are two independent, duplicated implementations of the order-created webhook sender (webhookSender.ts and legacyImportSender.ts) instead of one shared function/schema, which is why the legacy path silently drifted out of sync with the v2 contract instead of being forced to update.

The webhook payload has no explicit version field or schema-validation step on the sender side, so a sender can emit a payload that violates the documented contract (missing a 'v2, always present' field) with no error, warning, or build-time check catching it.

The documentation's claim that currency is 'always present' is not actually true/enforced across all code paths that produce this webhook, i.e., the docs describe an aspirational contract rather than one the sending code guarantees.

The partner-side consumer was written trusting the docs at face value with no defensive handling (e.g., default currency, optional chaining, or explicit validation/error on missing required field) for a payload that a producer-side bug can violate.
